Anne — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise summary you can use in the supplier assessment. I've kept the language practical and included callouts for exceptions and customer controls.

--- Summary (Redwood Inference: default hosted retention behaviors) ---
1) Default retention windows (hosted API, unless customer overrides via contract or private deployment):
   - Raw requests / user prompts: retained for 30 days. Stored to support debugging, billing reconciliation, and quality monitoring.
   - Model-generated outputs (complete responses): classified as derivative artifacts; retained for 90 days by default unless the output contains PII or a customer requests otherwise.
   - Streaming token fragments / ephemeral KV cache: not persisted for >72 hours in the default hosted configuration. Continuous streaming buffers are transient; persistent KV entries used for session resumption may be kept up to 30 days if enabled.

2) Treatment differences and exportability:
   - Prompts (original user inputs) and outputs (model-generated text) are treated as distinct classes: prompts are considered source requests; outputs are derivatives. Both are exportable on request, but export formats differ (raw request logs vs. rendered response bundles). Exports are subject to residency constraints.

3) Deletion workflow and SLAs:
   - Standard expiry: automated purge runs every 24 hours; data past its retention window is marked for deletion and removed from primary storage within 24–48 hours.
   - Customer-initiated purge (self-serve delete API): available for customers on Dedicated and Private plans. For hosted customers, deletion can be requested via support ticket or DPO request and Redwood aims to complete deletion within 5 business days across active replicas.
   - Backups / immutable snapshots: immutable backups are rotated on a 90‑day rotation schedule for hosted tiers; data subject to deletion is included in the next eligible rotation and pruned per our backup retention policy. For urgent legal/erasure claims we execute a documented remap-and-tombstone procedure; full cryptographic erasure is performed where supported by the underlying storage layer.

4) Residency controls (EU):
   - For hosted accounts that select EU residency, logs and derivative artifacts are stored in designated EU regions by default. Customers can request region-locking during onboarding or via contract amendment. Some short-lived operational metadata (control-plane traces) may transit other regions but are not retained beyond the stated windows.

5) Exceptions and legal holds:
   - Redwood may retain items beyond the standard windows under legal hold, active incident investigation, or when required by law. In such cases customers are notified and the retention extension is scoped to the minimum necessary.

Next steps:
- If BrightBank needs an SLA-backed delete API we can document an offering for Dedicated capacity or an enterprise add-on.
- If you'd like a one-page PDF summary tailored to your procurement team, say the word and I'll drop a signed copy.

Attachments: small retention matrix (internal), link to public retention doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/policies/data-retention-v2

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min call if you prefer to walk through specifics.

—Kimberly Park
